answer: Sybil resistance can run on copper, not paper: standing is wired through real, costly collaboration, and trust conducts only along wires that have already carried verifiable work. Every action sends a ripple to neighbours who can inspect it, so a fake identity's ripple dies out instead of spreading. A sybil farm may raise a big plume of activity, but smoke without fire cools fast: auditors check whether the plume traces back to real heat, completed tasks, and fakes that cannot show it lose their wiring.
